Commentary.Commentary: The West Indies innings is underway with Amir Jangoo and Kyle Mayers at the crease. Dipendra Singh Airee is set to bowl the first over for Nepal. The Nepal players have taken up their fielding positions, and the stage is set for an exciting contest between the two teams. Can Windies chase down 149? Or will Nepal defend this and cause an upset? Let's find out.
... The Run Chase ...

As the Windies prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Nepalis' bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stay tuned as the first delivery of the second inning is not far away.

The Nepalis lost four of their top batters in just 13 overs, putting 89 on the board, the remaining players in the batting order scrambled to boost the score as much as possible. However, the Windies bowlers excelled in the death overs, executing their strategies effectively to prevent any boundaries from being scored. Their disciplined performance kept the pressure on the batting side and limited their scoring opportunities.

Gulshan Jha is up for a chat and expresses that he enjoyed his time playing with the team, expressing excitement for future matches. He noted that the boundary wasn't particularly large, but he was waiting for the right delivery to capitalize on, referring to it as 'his zone ball'. With a good score to their name, Jha is optimistic about what's to come.

After losing two openers in quick succession, skipper Rohit Paudel and Kushal Bhurtel rose to the occasion to anchor the innings. They put together a vital partnership, adding 58 crucial runs to the scoreboard and stabilizing the situation. However, as they began to unleash their big shots, Navin Bidaisee was brought into the attack and quickly turned the tide. He effectively handled the threat, claiming the wickets of both batters in swift succession. First, Kushal Malla fell to his impressive bowling, followed by Rohit Paudel just a couple of overs later.

What an outstanding performance by the West Indies! A massive shoutout to Jason Holder and Navin Bidaisee, who truly deserve the admiration of every cricket fan for their incredible bagging 4 and 3 scalps respectively! Their exceptional bowling put relentless pressure on the Nepal batters and for that, the Windies were able to restrict their opposition to 148 runs for 8 wickets.

Another drop from Jewel Andrew at cover this time and Sompal Kami adds two to the total. Good length around off, Sompal Kami swings and slices this right over Jewel Andrew at cover. The fielder gets underneath it but his casual approach costs Obed McCoy a wicket as the ball goes in his grasp and pops out. Two runs taken. Nepal finishes with 148 for 8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to begin! The two umpires have taken their position and the players of the West Indies have scattered to take their fielding positions. Aasif Sheikh and Kushal Bhurtel will open for Nepal. Akeal Hosein will bowl with the new ball. Here we go...

We are just a few minutes away from the action to get underway. But before that, both sets of players and the match officials are getting lined up and as per the visuals, they are having a one-minute silence to pay tribute to those who have lost ltheir ives in Nepal. Now, it's time for national anthems. It will be the West Indies' first, followed by the Nepal national anthem.

West Indies coach Rayon Griffith expressed his excitement about the upcoming series, particularly for the young players in the squad. He highlighted Ackeem Auguste's promising performances and noted the team's efforts to strengthen their spin department with two leg-spinners. Griffith also emphasized the importance of the series against Nepal, mentioning the busy schedule ahead.

Nepal captain Rohit Paudel said that losing the toss wouldn't be a bad thing, given Sharjah's track record, where teams batting first have had success, such as in the previous tri-series. He expressed his team's excitement and pride in playing their first bilateral series against a full member side, especially against the two-time World Champions West Indies. The team is feeling positive and ready for the challenge.

West Indies captain Akeal Hosein expressed his desire to bowl first, citing the need to assess the pitch's offerings. After a couple of underwhelming series, Hosein emphasized the importance of winning this series to boost morale ahead of the World Cup. On his first stint as captain, Hosein said it's a great feeling to lead the West Indies and looks forward to the new opportunity. The team has made some changes, omitting Jediah Blades, Zishan Motara, Karima Gore, and one other player.
West Indies (Playing XI) - Kyle Mayers, Ackeem Auguste, Keacy Carty, Amir Jangoo (WK), Jewel Andrew, Jason Holder, Fabian Allen, Navin Bidaisee, Akeal Hosein (C), Ramon Simmonds, Obed McCoy.
Nepal (Playing XI) - Rohit Paudel (C), Sundeep Jora, Aasif Sheikh (WK), Kushal Bhurtel, Karan KC, Kushal Malla, Dipendra Singh Airee, Gulshan Jha, Sompal Kami, Nandan Yadav, Lalit Rajbanshi.
TOSS - West Indies have won the coin flip and they have elected to BOWL first.

The West Indies, led by Akeal Hosein, brings a youthful squad filled with promising talent, including five uncapped players vying for their T20 international debuts. With experienced players like Jason Holder, Fabian Allen, and Obed McCoy guiding the side, this series presents an opportunity for the youngsters to shine and make a name for themselves. Can Nepal spring a surprise and stun the West Indies, or will the Windies' new look side assert their dominance? We shall know soon. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Nepal, captained by Rohit Paudel and featuring star leg-spinner Sandeep Lamichhane, is looking to make the most of its first-ever bilateral series against a full member nation. With familiar names like Karan KC, Gulshan Jha, Sompal Kami, and Lalit Rajbanshi in the squad, Nepal is poised to put up a strong fight. The return of Mohammad Aadil Alam, who last played for Nepal in 2022, adds depth to the team.

The Nepal vs West Indies T20I series is set to kick off at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium, with the West Indies looking to assess their squad depth ahead of the Men's T20 World Cup. Their team boasts exciting young talents like Jewel Andrew and Kyle Mayers, who promise aggressive starts, while newcomers Amir Jangoo and Ackeem Auguste bring valuable CPL experience. Seasoned players Jason Holder and Fabian Allen add depth to the squad, alongside a pace-bowling trio of Shamar Springer, Obed McCoy, and Jediah Blades competing for a World Cup spot. Captain Akeal Hosein will also play a key role. In contrast, Nepal faces a tough challenge after struggling with inconsistency, particularly in their recent tri-series against the Netherlands and Scotland. Led by Rohit Paudel, Nepal's batting lineup will rely on crucial contributions from Aarif Sheikh and Dipendra Singh Airee, while the bowling department will be spearheaded by spinner Sandeep Lamichhane. This series promises to be thrilling, pitting the relatively new-look West Indies side against the rising Nepal team, offering fans a treat with both teams showcasing their skills.
